people.name: Antony the Great (Antony of Egypt)
people.summary: Egyptian Christian who withdrew to the desert c. 270-285 and became the archetypal hermit and 'father of monks'; Athanasius' Life of Antony spread his fame and the monastic ideal across the Christian world.

people.name: Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin
people.summary: Indigenous (Nahua) convert to whom, according to tradition first published in 1648-49, the Virgin of Guadalupe appeared at Tepeyac in 1531. His historicity is debated by historians; he was canonised by John Paul II in 2002.

people.name: Jean Cavalier
people.summary: Huguenot baker's apprentice who became a leading commander of the Camisard revolt in the Cévennes (1702-04), in a movement inspired by ecstatic prophets; after negotiating with Marshal Villars he went into exile and ended his life as a British officer and lieutenant-governor of Jersey.
keyIdeas: Armed resistance to persecution of Huguenots
Prophetic inspiration in the Camisard war

people.name: Barton W. Stone
people.summary: Presbyterian minister who hosted the Cane Ridge camp meeting (1801), then left the Presbyterian synod and led the 'Christian' movement that merged in 1832 with Alexander Campbell's Disciples to form the Stone-Campbell Restoration Movement.
keyIdeas: Christian unity on the Bible alone
Rejection of creeds as tests of fellowship

people.name: Seraphim of Sarov
people.summary: Russian monk and hermit of the Sarov monastery, famed as a spiritual elder, healer and teacher of the 'acquisition of the Holy Spirit'; canonised in 1903. Born in Kursk; his birth year is given as 1754 or 1759.
keyIdeas: Acquisition of the Holy Spirit as the aim of Christian life

people.name: Bernadette Soubirous
people.summary: Miller's daughter from Lourdes who reported eighteen apparitions of the Virgin Mary in 1858; she later became a Sister of Charity at Nevers and was canonised in 1933.

people.name: Agnes Ozman
people.summary: Student at Charles Parham's Bethel Bible School in Topeka who, on 1 January 1901, became the first in Parham's circle to speak in tongues, an event central to the formulation of the Pentecostal 'initial evidence' doctrine.
keyIdeas: Tongues as evidence of Spirit baptism

people.name: Pandita Ramabai Sarasvati
people.summary: Marathi Brahmin Sanskrit scholar who became a Christian (baptised 1883), campaigned for women's education and founded the Mukti Mission at Kedgaon for widows and orphans, where a revival broke out in 1905; she translated the Bible into Marathi.
keyIdeas: Women's education and rights in India

people.name: Gil Seon-ju (Kil Sun-ju)
people.summary: Korean Presbyterian elder and later one of the first seven ordained Korean pastors (1907), whose public confession helped spark the Pyongyang Great Revival; credited with the Korean practice of daybreak prayer and a signatory of the 1919 March First independence declaration.

people.name: Lúcia dos Santos
people.summary: Eldest of the three shepherd children of Fátima (with her cousins Francisco and Jacinta Marto, d. 1919 and 1920) who reported Marian apparitions in 1917; she became a Carmelite nun and wrote the Memoirs that are the main source for the 'secrets'.
keyIdeas: Devotion to the Immaculate Heart of Mary

people.name: Pio of Pietrelcina (Padre Pio)
people.summary: Italian Capuchin who reported receiving the stigmata in 1918 and became one of the most popular and controversial figures of 20th-century Catholicism; investigated repeatedly by the Holy Office, he was canonised in 2002.

people.name: Kathryn Kuhlman
people.summary: American evangelist whose 'miracle services' (from 1947) and television programme made her a leading healing evangelist; she credited healings to the Holy Spirit rather than herself and helped bridge Pentecostal and mainline/Catholic audiences.
keyIdeas: Healing by the sovereign work of the Holy Spirit

people.name: William Marrion Branham
people.summary: American healing evangelist who catalysed the post-war healing revival (1946-55); his later teachings (Oneness baptism, 'serpent seed', his own role as end-time prophet) are rejected by most Pentecostals and lie outside historic Nicene orthodoxy, but 'Message' churches still follow him.

people.name: John Arnott
people.summary: Canadian pastor who, with his wife Carol, led the Toronto Airport Vineyard (later Toronto Airport Christian Fellowship / Catch the Fire), home of the 'Toronto Blessing' from 1994.

people.name: Randy Clark
people.summary: American Vineyard pastor whose January 1994 meetings in Toronto started the 'Toronto Blessing'; he later founded Global Awakening, emphasising healing and impartation.

people.name: Steve Hill
people.summary: American Assemblies of God evangelist, previously a missionary in Argentina, whose Father's Day 1995 sermon at Brownsville Assembly of God in Pensacola launched the Brownsville Revival.

people.name: Joseph Ayo Babalola
people.summary: Yoruba evangelist whose 1930 revival at Ilesa, marked by healings and the burning of traditional objects, was central to the Aladura movement; he became the first spiritual leader of the Christ Apostolic Church.

people.name: Simeon Nsibambi
people.summary: Ugandan Anglican layman whose 1929 meeting with Joe Church helped spark the East African Revival; he emphasised repentance, holiness and 'walking in the light'.

people.name: John Edward (Joe) Church
people.summary: English Anglican (CMS Ruanda Mission) medical missionary at Gahini, Rwanda, who with Simeon Nsibambi was a leading figure of the East African Revival.

people.name: Sadhu Sundar Singh
people.summary: Sikh-born Indian Christian who reported a vision of Christ in 1904, became a wandering sadhu evangelist across India, Tibet and beyond, and was famous in Europe in the 1920s; he disappeared in the Himalayas in 1929.

people.name: John Sung (Song Shangjie)
people.summary: Chinese evangelist with a US doctorate in chemistry who led revival and healing campaigns across China and Southeast Asia (1927-1940), founding many evangelistic bands and shaping independent Chinese Protestantism.

people.name: Carlos Annacondia
people.summary: Argentine businessman turned evangelist whose mass campaigns from the early 1980s, with an emphasis on deliverance from demons and healing, were central to the Argentine revival.

people.name: Gunnar Vingren
people.summary: Swedish-born Baptist pastor turned Pentecostal who, with Daniel Berg, founded what became the Assembleias de Deus in Brazil after arriving in Belém in 1910.

people.name: Daniel Berg
people.summary: Swedish-born Pentecostal missionary who co-founded the Assembleias de Deus in Brazil with Gunnar Vingren, supporting the work partly as a foundry worker and colporteur.
